ANIMAL CATEGORIES LESSON · ANIMAL CATEGORIES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Fish — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the water-breathers, one fish at a time.

What is this?

Fish are the animals that live their whole lives underwater: they breathe water through gills, swim with fins and wear scales like armor.

What does it mean?

Different world, different breathing: we could not breathe water, a fish cannot breathe air — gills versus lungs is the first great animal split children can name.

What does the child need to know?

Gills are the fish’s lungs — water goes in the mouth, over the gills, out the sides; salmon are born in rivers, swim to the ocean, and find their home river again years later; goldfish are the famous bowl fish (and remember more than people think); catfish feel for food with whiskers.

Why this matters

Fish are the first pets many children meet, and the aquarium is the first ecosystem they can watch whole: feeding, cleaning, the circle complete.

What it teaches

Early biology (gills, fins, scales as vocabulary), the journey story (salmon homing) as first epic narrative, and empathy-through-care for a bowl or tank.

Words to learn

fishgillsfinsscalessalmongoldfishpiranhacatfishwhiskersshoal

Say this to your child

“"Fish breathe water! In the mouth, out the gills. The salmon swims across the whole ocean and still finds its home river, the goldfish knows dinner time, the piranha likes fruit more than fingers, and the catfish tastes the mud with its whiskers!"”

Step by step

  1. The gill demo: open your mouth wide and "breathe water" — in the mouth, out the sides. That is a fish’s whole breathing life.
  2. The salmon: born in a river, swims to the sea, grows big — then swims home to the exact river bend where it hatched. No map. Scientists still argue how.
  3. The goldfish: the bowl companion — it learns when feeding time is, and its memory is measured in months, not seconds.
  4. The piranha: famous teeth — but it mostly eats seeds and fruit; the monster story is mostly movie.
  5. The catfish: the bottom-feeler — whiskers that taste the muddy water, finding dinner in the dark.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the salmon arcs mid-jump, the goldfish has the biggest tail, the piranha shows its underbite and the catfish trails its whiskers below. Count the fins on each fish — every one is a steering wheel.

Ask your child

"What do fish breathe?" (water, through gills) "Which fish swims home to the river it was born in?" (the salmon) "Which fish has whiskers?" (the catfish)

What your child can say or do

Your child might breathe-water-demonstrate at bath time for a week, adopt the goldfish as a personal client with a feeding schedule, or refuse the piranha monster story with a firm "seeds and fruit".

Out in the real world

Salmon runs in Canada and the US Northwest (and the UK’s rivers) are visible from bridges in autumn — leaping fish, real and huge. Aquarium visits put every card fish within a pane of glass.

Try it together

Fish-y yoga: the goldfish wiggle (lie on back, wiggle all four fins), then fin-glides around the room with hands folded into a tail fin, bubble noises on. End with the salmon leap over a cushion waterfall.

Understanding check

Ask: "How does a fish breathe?" (water through its gills) "What covers a fish’s body?" (scales) "What does the catfish use whiskers for?" (tasting the water for food)

This lesson pairs with the Fish flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Animal Categories.
